props.title: Drowning Mona
props.initialSlug: Small-town murder mystery turns darkly comic farce

sections.content: Drowning Mona stands as a quirky dark comedy that blends small-town murder mystery with absurdist humor, following the pattern of oddball ensemble crime films like Fargo (1996) and To Die For (1995). Director Nick Gomez crafts a deliberately off-kilter world where everyone in Verplanck, New York drives a Yugo, and Bette Midler delivers one of her most acidic performances as the universally hated Mona Dearly. The film's strength lies in its stellar character actor ensemble, including Danny DeVito, Neve Campbell, Jamie Lee Curtis, and Will Ferrell in an early role.

sections.content: The film fits into a specific late 90s/early 2000s trend of darkly comic murder mysteries set in small towns, where the death of an unlikeable character reveals community secrets. Similar examples include Gossip (2000) and Drop Dead Gorgeous (1999), which use death as a lens to examine small-town dynamics and hidden resentments. The film's structure, revealing Mona's awful behavior through flashbacks, creates a "good riddance" murder mystery where nearly everyone had motive. SUBHEAD: Small Town Murder Comedy Evolution

While Drowning Mona wasn't a massive hit, it influenced later small-town murder comedies like Hot Fuzz (2007) and Bernie (2011). The film's approach to making every character simultaneously suspicious and sympathetic became a template for mixing mystery with dark humor. Its use of an ensemble cast where everyone's a viable suspect influenced works like Knives Out (2019).
